YouTube’s “Altered or synthetic content” label: when it appears and what metadata has to do with it

YouTube labels come from two places: what you declare in YouTube Studio, and metadata inside the video file. Here is how each one works, and how to check and clean what your MP4 or MOV carries before uploading.

Updated 2026-11-26 · 4 min read
Short answer: YouTube shows “Altered or synthetic content” mainly when the creator ticks the disclosure in YouTube Studio for realistic AI content, and it can add labels itself, for example for videos made with its own AI tools. Separately, it reads C2PA Content Credentials, for instance to show “Captured with a camera”. Cleaning metadata removes what the file says about itself; it does not change what you declare in Studio.

Two different sources

  • Your disclosure: when you upload, YouTube Studio asks whether the video contains realistic altered or synthetic content. Answering yes adds the label. For realistic AI content this disclosure is required.
  • Metadata in the file: YouTube reads C2PA Content Credentials. Videos from compatible cameras can show “Captured with a camera”; AI tools can write records that say the video was generated.

Check what your video carries

  1. Open IA Cleaner → Video and drop the MP4 or MOV.
  2. The report lists location, device, editing apps, XMP and Content Credentials, and the box What the original reveals shows any AI use recorded in them.
  3. If you want to upload without that data, download the clean copy. Frames are not re-encoded, so quality stays the same.

Things to keep in mind

  • Removing Content Credentials also removes “Captured with a camera”: keep them if you want to prove a video is authentic.
  • Cleaning metadata doesn’t change YouTube’s rules: realistic AI content still has to be disclosed in Studio.
  • A very common reason to clean is privacy: phone videos often carry the GPS location where they were recorded.

What IA Cleaner detects and removes

In videos (MP4, MOV) it identifies and removes recording location, device and app data, XMP and C2PA Content Credentials, without re-encoding a single frame. You see the full report first — every block found, with AI-related ones flagged — and then download the clean copy.
